Standard: The integrated air system operates as intended in the natural and induced environments it will encounter for its service life. TABLE I lists the environments assessed in this criterion. TABLE I. Natural and induced environments for the air system. Environment Natural, Induced, or Both Notes Temperature Natural and Induced Includes the ambient temperatures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes, thermal loading from subsystems and components of the air system, and cooling considerations. Temperature shock Induced Pressure Natural and Induced Static and dynamic pressures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes. Rapid decompression Induced Solar radiation (sunshine) Natural and Induced Includes the combination of natural environment forcing functions and the physical and chemical characteristics of the materiel itself. Wind speed and wind shear Natural Humidity Natural and Induced Rainfall Natural Includes identification of any areas for water intrusion, such as open doors and seepage through the air vehicle outer skin. Blowing snow and snow load Natural Icing conditions and freeze-thaw cycles Natural TABLE I. Natural and induced environments for the air system – Continued. Environment Natural, Induced, or Both Notes Sand and dust Natural Salt fog and corrosive environments Natural and Induced Includes gunfire gases, missile gases, sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Acceleration (Environment characterization) Induced Addresses the steady-state inertia loads induced by platform acceleration, deceleration, and maneuver in the service environment, including crash landing loads (static acceleration test). Vibration (Environment characterization) Induced Includes mechanical and gunfire vibration. Sonic fatigue (Environment characterization) Induced Includes all sources of acoustic loads. Shock (Environment characterization) Induced Addresses the materiel’s ability to physically and functionally withstand the shocks encountered in handling, transportation, and service environments including crash situations (transient shock test). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) The TEMP and the Environmental TEMP, as specified in MIL-STD-810, TEMP paragraph, contain the planned verification activities and testing environments to comprehensively address required levels of AW for the defined environment. Verification activities include any subset of service life testing to support entry into flight test and the tailored MIL-STD-810 requirements.
(2) Systems engineering planning and specification documentation account for variations and deviations in operating environment for air systems reliant upon DoW Component AW authority-accepted design approvals (e.g., FAA type design approval for CDA). At the discretion of the issuing authority, the variations and deviations do not invalidate the underlying design approval. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis of available environment verification data for the air system and its components, as collected in this section, confirms air system operation in all intended natural and induced environments. While the analysis addresses any available environment verification data, the minimum data set addresses twice the intended duration of flight test and the environment to be encountered during flight test. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment and showing no increased risk to operations. Examples of environment verification data: test data, drawings, digital twins of the air system, specification sheets, and ICDs. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Analysis.
  (2) Analysis of environment verification data for the air system and its components, as collected in this section, confirms air system operation in all intended natural and induced environments. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment and showing no increased risk to operations. Examples of environment verification data: test data, drawings, digital twins of the air system, specification sheets, and ICDs. Test.
    (1) Flight or Ground test: Air system testing verifies operations for natural and induced environmental conditions as defined in environment criteria documentation, the TEMP, and the Environmental TEMP. In addition to the test data showing operation in the natural and induced environment, data collected validates or substantiates modeling and analysis, including life cycle analysis. Testing may be conducted in full-scale climatic laboratories and in naturally occurring environments.
